sections.COMMENTS:
The Dinarides are a wide NW-SE fold-and-thrust belt stretching from southwestern Slovenia to Montenegro along the Adriatic coast of Croatia and inland. The Dinarides formed as a consequence of subduction and collision processes in the border zone between Europe and Adria tectonic plates. Adria acted, and is still acting, as an indenter moving roughly towards stable Europe and causing the Meso-Cenozoic carbonate rocks of the Dinaric platform to over-ride onto the Adriatic lithosphere (e.g. Aljinovic et al., 1990; Prelogovic et al., 1995; Herak, 1999). The most prominent structures of the Dinarides are NW-SE oriented thrust faults (Mamuzic, 1975; Ivanovic et al., 1976; Herak, 1991, 1999;). Present day tectonic rates are mostly obtained from GPS campaigns and display general NNE-SSW to NE-SW trends, with values of 2-2.5 mm/yr in northern Dalmatia (Grenerczy et al., 2005) and 4-4.5 mm/yr in central and southern Dinarides (Grenerczy et al., 2005; Bennett et al., 2008; Devoti et al., 2008).
Within the Dinarides the seismicity is distributed along the entire length of the belt. Data on both instrumental and historical seismicity show earthquake activity across the entire width of the thrust belt. Available focal mechanism solutions (Herak et al., 1995; Vannucci et al., 2004) and structural geological data show, that at its NW end the seismic deformation is dominated by right-lateral movement on NW-SE strike-slip faults. In the central and southern part of the belt, both in the off-shore and coastal parts, thrusting is the prevailing mode of seismic deformation whereas in the inner parts of the belt the fault planes are steeper and show more complex kinematics with reverse, strike-slip and oblique movements. Active processes in this region are mainly driven by NE oriented compression, documented from maximum compressive axis orientation of focal mechanisms (Anderson and Jackson, 1987; Pondrelli et al., 2006) and from long-term geological evidence (Prelogovic et al., 2003).
This Source is a NW-SE oriented reverse fault. The fault stretches from the area of Rijeka along the eastern outskirts of the Bakar Bay down to the Vinodol Valley.
We set the depth interval of the source taking into account data on characteristics of active seismogenic zones in the region (Kuk et al., 2000) and data used for seismic zonation (MarkuÅ¡ic and Herak, 1999). The strike of the source was derived by taking into consideration geologic data on fault geometry (BlaÅ¡kovic, 1999), combined with data on geomorphology and field observations. We obtained the average dip and rake of the source considering structural data (BlaÅ¡kovic, 1999) and regional tectonic characteristics (Tari and Pamic, 1998; Prelogovic et al., 2003). Such orientation fairly agrees with the orientation of the maximum horizontal compressive stress from GPS data in the region (Altiner et al., 2008).
We interpreted the local depth variations of a submerged notch with respect to the regional average trend (Benac et al., 2004; Benac et al., 2008) as due to the Vinodol fault displacement. Using age constraints on the notch provided by other studies (Marino and Pigorini, 1969; Å egota and Filipic, 1991) we obtained slip rate values. We also took into cosideration data of horizontal velocities obtained by GPS campaigns (Grenerczy et al., 2005) combined with the geometrical characteristics of the source.

pictures.t: Seismotectonic cross-section through the off-shore and coastal areas in Kvarner-Vinodol area
pictures.c: Regional seismtectonic cross-section throught the area of Kvarner bay through the area of Cres and Krk islands off-shore and Vinodol valley inland continuing well into inland parts of northern Croatian teritory, based on earthquake distribution and geological characteristics (Kuk et al. [2000]). Vinodol seismogenic source lies on a steeply dipping fault with reverse to reverse - strike-slip oblique kinematics.

pictures.t: Map of depth of submerged notch in the Kvarner bay
pictures.c: Position of depth of the submerged notch in the area of Kvarner bay (data of depth position taken from Benac et al. [2004]; Benac et al. [2008] and double-checked by field measurements). At the entrance of Bakar bay, that lies at the centre of the Vinodol seismogenic source, there is an abrupt change in the regional depth of submerged notch, displaying local differences of 52-58 cm confined to NW-SE oriented patch at the entrance to the bay. Position of the marine notches are a good indicator of active coastal processes connected to active displacements of the coasts or/and changes in sea-level. The number on the left side photo shows height of the submerged notch from the sea-floor.
